Galitsky, C., Worrell, E. and Ruth, M. (2003). Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Corn Wet Milling Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Report LBNL-52307, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, July 2003. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). ENERGY STAR measure catalogue; almost every number is reprinted (named in each note). Main file: Table 5 process-step energy for a modern 100,000 bu/day corn wet mill (14 steps plus the plant total), loaded as final electricity (kWh/t), steam and direct fuel (GJ/t) per t of CORN GROUND, converted from per-day kWh and Btu/bu with the source's own factors (1 bu = 25.4 kg; 1,250 Btu/lb steam) and exact Btu; dryer/evaporator energy per t of WATER EVAPORATED (germ steam-tube dryer 120% and 1.4 lb/lb, flash dryer 1350 Btu/lb, evaporator 0.4 lb/lb, Table 11 one to five effects, Sunmore MVR 0.032 kWh/kg, beet pulp press and rotary dryer); Table 10 dryer efficiencies; Table 12 MVR vs RO+MVR electricity per gallon of steepwater; molecular sieve vs rectification energy per gallon of ethanol; steam-turbine and gas-turbine CHP efficiencies and power-to-heat ratios (HHV); STIG size; Cerestar MVR incremental capex; CPC fluidized-bed germ dryer capex and lifetime; Ogilvie anaerobic effluent treatment capex per kW biogas. _measures.csv: quantified cross-cutting and process measures (Sect. 5.1-5.8). _other-values.csv: Table 5 primary energy, Table 4 sector energy, yields (Tables 2-3), Figure 9 printed shares, press power ratings, and values with unit errors. Not loaded: Figures 1-3, 7-8 read from charts; lighting and HVAC case studies from other industries; qualitative future technologies (enzymes, IMDS, gaseous SO2, alkali steeping, corn hybrids) except their cost numbers in measures. No flows file: yields are per bushel of commodities absent from commodity.csv (corn, starch, gluten).

(1) Table 5 "kWh" column is kWh per day for the 100,000 bu/day plant (= HP x 17.9), not per bushel; the Btu/bu column confirms. (2) Table 12 thermal and primary energy printed in "TBtu" for 350,000 gal of steepwater - impossible magnitude. (3) p.24: 1,000,000 Nm3 natural gas "equivalent to 33 TBtu/year" (about 0.035 TBtu). (4) p.44: press savings "360 to 1500 kWh/bu" should be kWh/day. (5) p.43: molecular sieve said to use one eighth of the energy of rectification (4 vs 96 kBtu/gal is 1/24); electricity 0.02-0.03 Wh/gal implausibly low. (6) p.50: Cerestar MVR "21 MWh" for a unit size. (7) p.47: CHP exhaust "2660F (1300C)" (1300 degC is 2372 degF). (8) Energy spend $15-25 million/yr (p.1, p.60) vs $20-30 million (abstract). (9) Wiseman (2001) in Table 9 vs Wideman (2001) in text. (10) p.56 refers to Table 5 "on page 20" (it is p.14) and Section 5.8.3 for membranes. (11) No price year for most costs; CHP efficiencies HHV, CPC germ dryer saving LHV; other energy values have no heating-value basis. (12) McCain economizer cost printed "166,800" without currency.
